learning_outcomes.text: Knows the properties and operating principles of drive systems.
Knows the technological conditions for drive system requirements.
Can formulate basic requirements for selecting a drive system to meet technological requirements.
Can select basic devices for specific drive requirements.
Is aware of the responsibility for their own work within the context of team work, carrying out a larger (technological) task.

syllabus_topics: Technical and economic aspects of drive selection. Overview of modern electric drives considering their properties and capabilities in industrial applications. Practical examples of selecting electric motors, static converters, parameter settings for drive systems. Cooling in power electronic drive systems. Protections in power electronic drive systems.

Laboratory classes and design exercises. These activities consolidate and expand the knowledge conveyed during lectures. An important element is meetings with representatives of leading companies offering drive solutions, during which practical aspects of offer selection are discussed. The classes also include training in selecting settings and commissioning inverters, using specific company equipment.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must complete all laboratory exercises. Student presence at lectures is not explicitly stated as obligatory, but students are expected to participate and clarify doubts. For laboratory classes, students must be prepared for the exercise, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium, and present a solution to the problem.
